head_commit.message:
fix(analyzer): bind ONE hazm WordTokenizer — per-call re-read of words.dat hung CI

hazm 0.12.1's module-level word_tokenize() constructs WordTokenizer() on
EVERY call, and each construction re-reads and re-parses the full words.dat
(seconds per document). _init_hazm bound that module function, so the BM25
fit (30k Alef-region docs, up to 34k chars) and the vector ingest never
finished: three build-index-snapshot CI attempts died at the 360-min wall
with zero records ingested (attempt 1 died as 'runner lost communication —
starved for CPU').

Fix: construct one WordTokenizer at init and bind the instance method.
Token-equality vs the old path verified on normalized inputs (production
path = tokenize(normalize(text))) — identical vectors, identical snapshot.
Measured: BM25 fit on the exact CI fit sample: >6h (hang) -> 19s.
Bonus: query-time tokenization no longer re-reads words.dat per query.

head_commit.message:
fix(ci): feasible snapshot build — input-keyed cache, wired embed batch, ingest watchdog

- build-index-snapshot cache key was hashFiles(pins.json): the pin-fill
  commit itself changed the key, guaranteeing a cache MISS on the next run
  -> a second 6h rebuild -> strict sha256 re-verify fails on tar byte drift.
  Key now derives from the snapshot INPUTS (dataset commit + model revision
  + ingestion-code revision r1), stable across the pin-fill.
- DEHKHODA_EMBED_BATCH_SIZE was never wired: embed_documents hard-defaulted
  32, so the 312k-row e5 ingestion exceeded the 360-min hosted-runner wall
  (attempt 2 cancelled at 363 min). Now env-wired (vectors unchanged —
  batching affects throughput only).
- Ingest step now runs under a watchdog emitting the last checkpoint event
  to the job log every 10 min, so timeouts/infra kills leave evidence.

head_commit.message:
fix(ci): run deb-rename step under bash — ${var// /./} is bash-only

build-linux died at the new normalization step:

    /__w/_temp/...sh: 12: Bad substitution

The build-linux job's default shell is sh (dash) inside the container;
the bash-only parameter expansion ${f// /.} needs shell: bash. Same
pattern every other inline step in this job uses docker-run bash or
explicit shells.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(release): normalize .deb filename before hashing — release-page s…

head_commit.message:
fix(release): normalize .deb filename before hashing — release-page sha256sum -c parity

Phase E verification of the published v1.3.0 failed one line:

    sha256sum: './Dehkhoda RAG_1.3.0_amd64.deb': No such file or directory

Root cause: the tauri deb is named "${productName}_..." = 'Dehkhoda
RAG_1.3.0_amd64.deb' (space). SHA256SUMS.all hashed the on-disk name, and
the release job's in-CI parity check passed — but GitHub release assets
cannot contain spaces: on upload the asset silently became
'Dehkhoda.RAG_...deb' (dot), so the published sums referenced a name no
asset on the page has. The bytes themselves are authentic: the downloaded
.deb's sha256 matches the sums entry exactly; only the reference is wrong.

Fix: normalize the .deb to the GitHub asset name (space -> dot) in
build-linux immediately after appimage.sh, BEFORE any hashing (appimage
artifact sums, arch adapter, release-job SHA256SUMS.all). arch.sh's
version extraction (cut -d_ -f2) is unaffected.

Next release run replaces the published assets: same bytes, corrected
SHA256SUMS.all. No artifact content change.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(cli): report verified:true in lean model-step results

head_commit.message:
fix(cli): report verified:true in lean model-step results

All 4 lean appimage-acceptance jobs failed at the pins.json gate even
though verification itself passed:

    {"t":"result","step":"model","ok":true,"data":{"status":"ready",
     "dir":"...","source":"downloaded","revision":"..."}}
    model files did not verify against pins.json

The lean existing-dir branch ran verify_dir() (its ok:true proves the
hashes matched) but, unlike the full-variant branch, omitted
"verified": true from the emitted result — the acceptance script greps
for that flag. Same omission in the post-download branch.

Fix: include "verified": true in both lean result payloads (truthful:
verify_dir / per-file sha256 of the download just ran). Full-variant
payload unchanged; wizard UI unaffected (reads ok/status only).

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(events): ensure_ascii JSONL — cp1252 UnicodeEncodeError killed Wi…

head_commit.message:
fix(events): ensure_ascii JSONL — cp1252 UnicodeEncodeError killed Windows model gate

The de-blinded Windows gate (previous commit) exposed the real error:

    File "bootstrap\\events.py", line 20, in emit
        print(json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
    UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode characters

The wizard JSONL protocol carries Persian task_fa text over a piped
stdout; on Windows the child sidecar inherits the ANSI codepage (cp1252
on en-US runners) and print() dies at the first Persian progress event —
'Build gate: bundled model verify + real e5 dense probe' never ran the
dense probe at all.

Note: this is a latent real-app bug as well (no PYTHONIOENCODING is set
by backend_launcher or the Tauri side); on fa-IR Windows (cp1256) it
hides, on en-US Windows it would kill the wizard's model step. CI merely
surfaced it first because its locale is en-US.

Fix:
- events.emit: json.dumps default ensure_ascii=True -> pure-ASCII wire
  format; u06XX escapes round-trip losslessly through the wizard's
  JSON.parse (verified consumers: wizard-bridge.js x3), safe on every
  codepage
- bootstrap/tests/test_events_ascii.py: wraps stdout in a real cp1252
  TextIOWrapper, asserts no crash + ASCII-only wire + exact Persian
  round-trip incl. structured dl payload and error_fa; wired into
  windows-bootstrap
- release.yml Windows gates: also export PYTHONUTF8=1
  PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 as defense-in-depth

No user-facing behavior change: the wizard UI receives identical JSON
objects after JSON.parse in both variants.
